description: OmniClaude Core Hooks - OMN-13244 measurement baseline with the OMN-13856, OMN-14330, OMN-15062, OMN-15213, OMN-16277, OMN-16162, OMN-16471, OMN-16478, OMN-17006, and OMN-17168 carve-outs. Every context-injection/measurement hook stays DISABLED; the only re-registered hooks are the Done-flip durable-evidence guard (OMN-13856, operator-approved, no fake Done), the OMN-7018 worktree canonical-root guard (OMN-14330, blocks `git worktree add` outside $OMNI_HOME/omni_worktrees), the SubagentStop secret-leak guard (OMN-15062, blocks a subagent's final report from completing when it matches a known secret pattern -- narrowly scoped security control), the SubagentStop report-contract guard (OMN-15213, fails a lane RED when its final return is bare-Done-class instead of the report the golden-chain contract requires), the PostToolUse Bash-output secret-redaction guard (OMN-16277, masks secret-shaped patterns in raw Bash tool_response text via hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput before it lands in the transcript -- narrowly scoped security control, same class as OMN-15062, NOT a re-enable of the disabled context-injection/measurement hooks), the SessionStart/SessionEnd/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse(.*) bus-mirror hooks (OMN-16162, direct-dispatch a session-started/session-ended/prompt-submitted/tool-executed event to omnimarket's node_event_emit_effect, backgrounded and fail-open -- the local-bus-mirror transport superseding the OMN-16090 HTTP spool-shipper stopgap; S0 wired SessionStart/SessionEnd, S1 extends the identical pattern to UserPromptSubmit and a dedicated catch-all PostToolUse entry that never touches tool_response, kept separate from the OMN-16277 Bash-matcher secret-redaction guard), the OMN-16471 lane-death pair (PreToolUse on ^(Task|Agent|Workflow)$ records a durable OPEN lane record at the dispatch seam -- pure observer, always exit 0, always silent, so it can never refuse or delay a dispatch; SubagentStop classifies HOW the lane ended from transcript evidence -- tool-call count, wall duration, and the F-09 death signatures -- writes the paired terminal record, and blocks once on a zero-work death so `onex-lane-reconcile` can fail on any lane that has a dispatch record and no terminal one), and the PreToolUse SendMessage lane-liveness guard (OMN-16478, blocks a message that declares another lane dead or authorizes a takeover of its work unless an independent filesystem probe returns DEAD, and refuses a bare harness ref used as an address). None of these re-registrations is a re-enable of the disabled context-injection/measurement hooks. All other scripts remain on disk and re-registration stays a pure config change. Tenth carve-out: the PreToolUse overseer foreground-block guard (OMN-17006, re-registering the OMN-8376 guard that the OMN-13244 baseline unregistered -- blocks foreground Bash/Edit/Write/NotebookEdit/MultiEdit against repo paths while `$ONEX_STATE_DIR/overseer-active.flag` marks an overseer contract as driving, so the lead agent cannot drift into manual fixes; allows everything when the flag is absent). Its sibling from the same audit, the OMN-8928/8929 dispatch-claim pre/post pair, is DELIBERATELY NOT re-registered: its `exit 2` is swallowed by the error-guard EXIT trap (it never calls `trap - EXIT`), its deny payload uses a `{"type":"permissionDenied"}` shape this harness does not honour, and its claimant falls back to the shared constant `session`, so two anonymous lanes can never collide. Both scripts stay on disk, unregistered; OMN-17005 carries the four re-registration ACs and the expiry condition (unmet identity AC => close won't-fix and delete, do not carry dead code). Authority for both decisions: docs/tracking/2026-08-29-beta-off-the-rails-analysis.md, mechanism A1. STANDING RULE (OMN-17006, from that report's addendum): any future baseline-style disable of a hook registered here MUST land in the same change as an expiry condition and a named re-enable ticket recorded in this description, and that record MUST name all four of: OWNER -- the person or lane accountable for restoring it; REASON -- why this specific hook is off, not merely that it is; EXPIRY -- the absolute condition or date after which the disable is void; RESTORATION -- the automatic behaviour that re-registers the hook once the expiry is reached, and the re-enable ticket that tracks it. A disable with no expiry and no re-enable ticket is how OMN-13244 left enforcement dark for months while the rule it enforced was corrected by hand ~61 times. Eleventh carve-out: the SessionStart goal-surface hook (OMN-17168, session_start_goal_surface.sh -- prints the `state_as_of` of $KNOWLEDGE_BASE_INTERNAL_PATH/beta/GOAL.md, its age, and the goal rows, and when that goal is missing or older than 12h prints the exact re-baseline command `Workflow({ name: 'morning-ground-state', args: { date: '<today>' } })`). It is print-only: pure bash with no interpreter, no network, no writes, no state, and it exits 0 on every user-visible outcome including a missing file and an unset env var, so it can neither refuse nor delay a session. Its one non-zero path (exit 3) is an existing-but-unreadable GOAL.md, reported with full absolute paths; exit 3 does not block SessionStart. KNOWLEDGE_BASE_INTERNAL_PATH has NO default (CLAUDE.md rule 8): a guessed clone path would surface another checkout's goal as if it were this one, so an unset variable prints the variable name and the expected value instead. It is not a re-enable of the disabled context-injection/measurement hooks -- it injects one artifact the session is already required to open from (memory feedback_session_goal_from_ground_state_reconciled_to_plan), not model-generated context. Per the STANDING RULE above, its own carve-out record: OWNER -- Jonah Gray / the session-goal lane; REASON -- the durable session goal is invisible at session start, so it is remembered rather than read, which is the same dark-enforcement class as OMN-13244 itself; EXPIRY -- when OMN-17169 lands the goal projection (ground-state EFFECTs -> reconcile COMPUTE -> goal REDUCER -> ORCHESTRATOR) and GOAL.md stops being the source of truth; RESTORATION -- at that expiry the hook is REPOINTED from the file read to the projection read and stays registered under this same entry; it is not unregistered, and OMN-17169 carries that repoint as a closeout AC. The named workflow is the acknowledged stopgap. Twelfth carve-out: the OMN-17207 LOCAL-CAPTURE pair — post_tool_use_auto_checkpoint.sh and post_tool_use_changeset_guard.sh — re-registered on a Bash matcher, LAST in PostToolUse order. Both are re-enables of hooks the OMN-13244 baseline unregistered, and both are revived as DURABLE LOCAL CAPTURE ONLY: they write to the local filesystem and emit NOTHING on stdout. auto-checkpoint writes ~/.claude/handoffs/checkpoint-<ts>.md on a `git commit` (commit sha, branch, message, diff --stat file count, active plan, PR number+state); changeset-guard appends one JSON line to ~/.claude/changeset-guard-events/events.jsonl when a commit exceeds 15 files. Three deliberate changes from the pre-OMN-13244 versions, each closing a defect the archaeology of 2026-08-30 found: (1) the `printf '%s' "$TOOL_INFO"` passthrough echo on every branch is REMOVED — plain PostToolUse stdout is debug-log-only, but echoing the payload back re-emits the raw tool_response that the OMN-16277 secret-redaction guard masks on this same Bash matcher; (2) changeset-guard's advisory context injection is NOT revived, only its JSONL side-write — per-turn injection is the token cost OMN-13244 removed, and the JSONL series was the only durable machine-readable output the entire pre-baseline hook surface ever produced (2,703 lines over 56 days); (3) auto-checkpoint's `gh pr view` is bounded by `timeout 5`, and its retention cap is raised from 5 to OMNICLAUDE_CHECKPOINT_RETENTION (default 200) — the 5-file cap is why only 5 checkpoints, all from one 8-hour window, survived to be examined. Neither hook publishes to the bus: that half stays gated behind OMN-17209, so this is not an OMN-16162-class transport re-enable. Registration order is pinned by test: these two come AFTER the secret-redaction guard, because updatedToolOutput is last-writer-wins and only a hook that emits the field can clobber it — these emit nothing. Per the STANDING RULE above, the OMN-17207 carve-out record: OWNER — Jonah Gray / the observability ladder lane (epic OMN-16176); REASON — the ledger records that a Bash ran for 265 ms but not that the tree changed, so every claim of work is unfalsifiable from the ledger; these two hooks restore the git-delta and changeset-magnitude fields locally while the bus half is designed; EXPIRY — when OMN-17207 (C11) lands work.delta events on the bus with the C10 identity block, and OMN-17209 clears the egress/redaction gate that keeps these payloads local today; RESTORATION — at that expiry these two hooks are SUPERSEDED, not merely unregistered: the checkpoint markdown and the JSONL series are replaced by work.delta events and their projection, and OMN-17207 carries that removal as a closeout AC so the local files cannot outlive the bus path and become a second, divergent authority.
